(p-333) Surah al-'Asr

Makkan. In one of the two reports from Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah, it is Madinan.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By the 'Asr﴾ This is an oath, and there are two views on it:

The first: that al-'asr is time (ad-dahr). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam.

The second: that it is the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy), the period between the sun's passing its zenith and its setting. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. To this belongs the poet's line:

"Set out with us in the afternoon, O 'Amr, for the 'asr has grown short; in the first evening journey lie gain and reward."

He singled it out for the oath because it contains the closing moments of deeds.

A third view is possible: that He means the era (asr) of the Messenger (ﷺ), because of its excellence through the renewal of prophethood in it.

A fourth view: that He means the 'Asr prayer, which is the middle prayer, because it is the most excellent of the prayers. This was said by Muqatil.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ By "mankind" (al-insan) He means the human race.

Concerning "loss" (khusr) there are four views: (p-334)

The first: in destruction. This was said by as-Suddi.

The second: in evil. This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

The third: in deficiency. This was said by Ibn Shajarah.

The fourth: in punishment. To this belongs His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the outcome of its affair was loss﴾. 'Ali (may God be pleased with him) used to recite it: "By the 'Asr and the vicissitudes of time, indeed mankind is in loss, and indeed he will remain in it until the end of time."

﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to the truth﴾ There are three interpretations of "the truth" (al-haqq): The first: that it is tawhid (the oneness of God). This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

The second: that it is the Qur'an. This was said by Qatadah.

The third: that it is God. This was said by as-Suddi.

A fourth is possible: that a person charges those he leaves behind, when death draws near, not to die except as Muslims.

﴿And urge one another to patience﴾ There are two views on it:

The first: patience in obedience to God. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: patience in what God has made obligatory. This was said by Hisham ibn Hassan.

A third interpretation is possible: patience in refraining from the forbidden things and from following desires.
